## TL;DR

This task improves first-run and failure guidance on Work and Agents. Work distinguishes a successfully empty project from a failed request, offers create-task and retry actions, and keeps both panels outside the responsive board columns. Load errors remain visible when status filters are active. The Agents page points projects with no configured roles toward built-in choices. This review pass also fixes concurrent refresh races so stale responses cannot replace the latest request's error or board snapshot.

## Work and rationale

The Work store tracks an initial task-load error separately from loading and task data. That distinction prevents a network failure from looking like an empty project. A successful empty response gets a first-task prompt and opens the existing create-task flow; a failed request gets readable server guidance and Retry. A successful retry clears the error. API transport errors use the shared friendly server-connection message.

The initial review found the two guidance panels were rendered as children of `.board`. That container lays out status columns as a flex row on wide screens and a three-column grid below 1250px, which squeezed the panels into a column-sized cell. I moved both sections into the Work page flow immediately before the board. The board's existing responsive layout now applies only to task columns. A filtered empty count still does not show the project-wide empty prompt, but an actual board-load error remains visible with or without a status filter.

The Agents page detects projects with no configured roles and presents a direct action to choose a built-in agent. Its fixture simulates the first-run state without persisting a configuration change. The Work fixtures cover successful empty and failed-load states.

Review round 2 identified that overlapping `refresh()` calls could set or clear `boardLoadError` in response-completion order. Each refresh now receives a monotonically increasing request id. Only the latest-started request can change the load error or hydrate the board snapshot. The `init()` catch still reports failures that occur before a board refresh starts, such as a failed health request, while yielding to any newer refresh.

## Approaches tried

I started the auth-less server from this task worktree and exercised Work and Agents at 1280×900 and 375×812 with Playwright WebKit. The empty and failed Work fixtures and the empty Agents fixture showed the expected guidance at both widths. Document width matched viewport width, and I observed no page or console errors. I also intercepted the live `/api/board` request to fail, verified the server guidance, clicked Retry, allowed the request through, and saw tasks return at both widths.

For the layout and filter findings, component tests assert both guidance sections are outside the `.board` container and that the error panel remains visible alongside a Ready filter. For the refresh race, deferred fetch promises make response ordering deterministic. Tests cover an old failure arriving after a successful retry and an old success arriving after the latest request has failed.

## Challenges and blockers

The computer-use browser bridge did not expose viewport controls or console output, so I used the repository's Playwright WebKit runner for the responsive and error-path checks. The first scoped check found a formatter issue in `AgentsView.vue`; I ran `bun run fmt` and reran it successfully. In this review pass, the two new refresh-race tests passed. The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` also passed: all 389 changed-path test files (5,589 tests, one skipped), build, format, lint, safety guards, contrast audit, and UI smoke.

## Key learnings

Conditional guidance should live outside the flex/grid container whose items it explains; otherwise responsive column rules can turn a callout into a narrow column. A status filter changes which tasks are visible, not whether the underlying request succeeded. For concurrent refreshes, response arrival order is not request authority: a request id lets the latest-started refresh own both the visible error and the board snapshot. Deferred promises make those timing guarantees testable without relying on nondeterministic delays.
